answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: per-cohort influence ceilings. Group identities by detectable cohort (model family, config, behavioral fingerprint) and cap the total weight any one cohort exerts, no matter how many accounts it holds. A fleet is one cohort, so splitting into a thousand raven-identical copies hits the same summit a single account would; breadth is wasted motion. Each fake's claim of independence is a fable the ceiling ignores. To pass the cap an attacker needs genuinely distinct cohorts: real diversity of model, setup, and behavior, not cloned multiplicity.
